title: ～さえ～ば — if only ～ / as long as ～
summary: Says that one condition alone is enough for the result: “if only ～, then ～; as long as ～.” さえ marks the one key element, and the verb or adjective ends in the ば-form. The second half is a result that follows once that condition is met.

patterns.form: 名詞＋さえ＋ば形（形容詞・名詞）
patterns.gloss: noun + さえ + ば-form (天気さえ良ければ)

patterns.form: 動詞ます形＋さえすれば
patterns.gloss: verb stem + さえすれば (飲みさえすれば)

body.p: With nouns and na-adjectives: あなたさえよければ. With i-adjectives: 安くさえあれば. With verbs: stem + さえすれば (飲みさえすれば). It carries the speaker's feeling that this one condition is enough and nothing else matters.

The second half is a result, possibility or state, such as 治る, できる or 大丈夫だ. An intention or command is hard to place there. A related pattern 〜さえ…ばいい means “that alone is fine,” and works for wishes and advice. Its feature is stressing that a single condition suffices.

examples.ja: 薬（くすり）を飲（の）みさえすれば、すぐ治（なお）ります。
examples.romaji: Kusuri o nomi sae sureba, sugu naorimasu.
examples.tr: If you just take the medicine, you'll get better soon.

examples.ja: あなたさえよければ、いつでも出発（しゅっぱつ）できます。
examples.romaji: Anata sae yokereba, itsu demo shuppatsu dekimasu.
examples.tr: As long as you're okay with it, we can leave anytime.
examples.note: Your readiness is the only condition.

examples.ja: 天気（てんき）さえ良（よ）ければ、明日（あした）は海（うみ）へ行（い）ける。
examples.romaji: Tenki sae yokereba, ashita wa umi e ikeru.
examples.tr: If only the weather is good, we can go to the sea tomorrow.

pitfalls: Verbs use stem + さえすれば: × 飲むさえすれば, ○ 飲みさえすれば.
Do not forget the ば-form: × 天気さえ良い、行ける.
